title: Саша переезжает к Максу и Косте  (Sasha Moves In with Max and Kostya)

segments.t: Feeling responsible for the flood, Max invites Sasha to move into his apartment with him and Kostya. Although Sasha first suspects he is only asking out of guilt, she happily accepts and starts kissing him right on the kitchen table as Kostya walks in.
Я сама разберусь со своими проблемами, правда.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'Listen, I have been thinking.' Max holds an earnest tack straight away, joining "slushay" ("listen") to "tut" ("here") so every word pulls its weight.
'Will you move in with me?' Kostya prompts bluntly without a pause, leaning on "pereydesh" ("to cross, switch") before closing the thought with "ty" ("you").
'You just feel guilty.' Max shows a direct rhythm right away, linking "chuvstvuyesh" ("feel"), "vinu" ("fault, guilt"), and "chto" ("what") in one brisk exchange.
Я сама разберусь со своими проблемами, правда.
'I can handle my own problems myself, really.' Sasha favors a wry style without hesitation, leaning on "razberus" ("I will sort out") before closing the thought with "problemami" ("problem").
'I am not asking because of that.' Max chooses a measured angle in this beat, leaning on "da" ("yes") before closing the thought with "ya" ("I").
'I have wanted to offer this to you for a long time.' Kostya chooses a steady posture during the exchange, joining "davno" ("for a long time") to "khotel" ("wanted") so every word pulls its weight.

'Well, are you sure about it yourself?' Max challenges openly to Kostya here, linking "uveren" ("sure, confident") directly with "nu" ("oh, come on"), since Russian drops "is" and "are" in the present.
'Why would I not be?' Kostya probes bluntly right away, using "chego" (from "chto", "what") alongside "net" ("no") to shape the meaning.
'Why am I wasting time for nothing?' Max probes wryly without hesitation, linking "zrya" ("for nothing"), "vremya" ("time"), and "teryayu" ("to lose") in one brisk exchange.
'Maybe right here?' Kostya asks sharply toward Sasha here, leaning on "mozhet" ("can") before closing the thought with "pryamo" ("right, just").
'Do not mind me.' Max adopts a wry attitude in front of Kostya, anchoring the Russian line on "obrashchayte" ("to turn, to direct") and "vnimaniya" ("attention") without extra filler.
'I did not see you two.' Kostya maintains an emphatic posture for Sasha, pairing "videl" ("saw, have seen") with "ya" ("I") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
'Kostik, close your eyes.' Max presents a steady posture in their talk, pairing "zakroy" ("shut, close") with "glaza" ("eyes") to get the point across in plain spoken Russian.
Я сама разберусь со своими проблемами, правда.
That wraps up this scene as max invites Sasha to move into his and Kostya's apartment, and she immediately makes herself at home while Kostya awkwardly walks in on them. Until next time!
